classes.description: Injectable or oral GLP-1/GIP agents labeled for chronic weight management (NOT their diabetes-labeled versions): semaglutide (Wegovy, including Wegovy tablets), tirzepatide (Zepbound), liraglutide (Saxenda). Many plans exclude weight-loss drugs entirely; an exclusion is a valid finding (outcome nonformulary).
classes.plainDescription: A weekly shot (or daily pill) for weight loss, like Wegovy or Zepbound.

paRequired.reason: Clinical criteria under NYRx DUR (page 75): diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea; BMI of 40 kg/m2 or greater; lifestyle modifications; two treatment attempts per lifetime
criteria: Indication: moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). NYRx lists no other indication for Zepbound, such as weight loss alone.
BMI of 40 kg/m2 or higher at initiation of therapy.
Tried CPAP or currently using a CPAP device (rationale required if not).
Completed polysomnography or a home sleep apnea test (rationale required if not).
Referred for a nutrition consult, with at least 6 months of comprehensive lifestyle modification before starting, continuing throughout treatment.
Within the lifetime limit of two treatment attempts.

records.stepTherapy: No step therapy listed. Lifetime quantity limit of two treatment attempts (page 75).
records.verificationNote: Read NYRx PDL page 75 (Drug Utilization Review table), where Wegovy and Zepbound are listed with clinical criteria. Wegovy is chosen as the pick because it is listed first and its criteria are the same barrier level as Zepbound; this is a judgment call, not a PDL designation. Saxenda (liraglutide) and Wegovy tablets do not appear on this PDL; the PDL is not complete (page 1), so their coverage is not determined here. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: spot-checked page 75: Wegovy BMI>=40, CVD diagnosis, lifestyle, 2 lifetime attempts; Zepbound OSA - match.]
preferredCriteria: Indication: established cardiovascular disease (form frames Wegovy as reducing major adverse cardiovascular events). NYRx lists no other indication, such as weight loss alone.
BMI of 40 kg/m2 or higher at initiation of therapy.
Adherent for at least 6 months before starting to CVD therapy: antihypertensive, lipid-lowering, and antithrombotic or platelet inhibitor (rationale accepted if not).
Prescriber attests comprehensive lifestyle modification (behavior change, reduced-calorie diet, more activity) began at least 6 months before starting and continues.
Within the lifetime limit of two treatment attempts.
